statements.text: a driver SHOULD NOT cut in front of a truck

sources.quote: Never cut in front of a truck. Cutting into the open space in front of a truck or bus removes the driver’s cushion of safety. Trying to beat a truck to a single-lane construction zone represents a particularly dangerous situation. Either slow down and exit or stay behind the truck.

statements.note: The heading (Cutting Off a Vehicle to Reach Your Exit or Turn) names the usual motive; the rule itself has no condition.

statements.text: a cyclist MUST ride as far to the right in the lane as [?possible] ONLY IF the lane can be shared [?safely] by a car and a bicycle side by side

sources.quote: Bicyclists are required to ride as far to the right in the lane as possible only when the lane can be shared safely by a car and a bicycle, side-by-side. Even then, there are certain conditions that allow a bicyclist to take the full lane.

flags.note: How far right is left to the cyclist's judgment.
When the lane can be shared safely is not said.

flags.span: ride as far to the right in the lane as possible
flags.note: Chapter 13 (p125) states this duty again with a different condition (moving slower than other traffic) and "as near as possible to the right curb or edge of the road".

statements.note: "Only when" is written as ONLY IF: the duty does not apply when the lane cannot be shared side by side, which decides whether a car can pass the bicycle within the lane.

statements.text: EXCEPTION TO p119a: a cyclist MAY take the full lane WHEN the cyclist is passing another vehicle going in the same direction

statements.text: a driver SHOULD WATCH FOR the other driver drifting in front of the passing vehicle WHEN passing a driver who [?seems] to be distracted BECAUSE the other driver may not be aware of the passing driver

sources.quote: Be very careful when passing a driver who seems to be distracted. The other driver may not be aware of your presence, and they may drift in front of you.

flags.note: How a driver seems distracted is left to judgment.

statements.note: The hazard (drifting in front) is named in the next sentence, so "Be very careful" is written as WATCH FOR.

statements.text: a cyclist MUST ride as near as [?possible] to the right curb or edge of the road WHEN the cyclist is moving slower than the other traffic on the road UNLESS the cyclist is passing another vehicle going in the same direction OR the cyclist is preparing for a left turn at an intersection or onto a private road or driveway OR there are [?unsafe] conditions in the road such as fixed or moving objects, parked or moving vehicles, pedestrians, animals, potholes or debris OR the cyclist is in an outside lane that is less than 14 ft wide and has no designated bicycle lane adjacent to that lane OR the cyclist is in an outside lane that is too narrow for a bicycle and a motor vehicle to travel [?safely] side by side

sources.quote: A person operating a bicycle who is moving slower than the other traffic on the road shall ride as near as possible to the right curb or edge of the road unless:
The person is overtaking and passing another vehicle proceeding in the same direction
The person is preparing for a left turn at an intersection or onto a private road or driveway
There are unsafe conditions in the road such as fixed or moving objects, parked or moving vehicles, pedestrians, animals, potholes, or debris, or

The person is operating a bicycle in an outside lane that is: Less than 14 feet in width and doesn’t have a designated bicycle lane adjacent to that lane; or The lane is too narrow for a bicycle and a motor vehicle to safely travel side by side.
When is a bicyclist not required to ride to the right of the roadway? (Chpt. 13)

flags.note: How near is left to the cyclist's judgment.

statements.text: a driver SHOULD NOT intentionally slow down, slam on the brakes or speed up to keep another road user from passing or from entering the driver's lane

sources.quote: Do not intentionally slow down, slam on your brakes, or speed up to keep someone from passing or entering your lane of travel.

flags.span: speed up to keep someone from passing

statements.note: From the road-rage tips; the lane-entry part is kept because it is in the same sentence.

statements.text: DEFINE a blind spot IS an area THAT the mirrors cannot show

sources.quote: blind spot – an area rearview mirrors cannot show

statements.note: The glossary says "rearview mirrors" (plural), written as the mirrors because the singular "rearview mirror" elsewhere means the inside mirror.

statements.text: DEFINE overtake IS to pass a vehicle THAT is ahead

sources.quote: overtake – to pass the vehicle ahead

statements.note: The other statements write "pass" wherever the handbook says "overtake", as this definition equates them.

statements.text: DEFINE a race IS the use of one or more vehicles THAT includes an attempt to outgain or outdistance another vehicle or to prevent another vehicle from passing

sources.quote: race – the use of one or more vehicles in an attempt to:
Out gain or outdistance another vehicle or prevent another vehicle from passing;

statements.note: Only the first item of the glossary list is among the passages, so the definition is written with "includes".
